notes: Batch N: atenolol, bisoprolol, propranolol, verapamil, diltiazem, nifedipine, lercanidipine. All quotes checked FOUND against fetched text (837 quotes). Source choices: the clinic monograph link for bisoprolol (emc 12963) returns 404; a generic UK bisoprolol 5 mg SmPC (emc-14905) was used, plus emc-101896 (lists only hypertension and angina; recorded as a detail item). No verapamil immediate-release tablet SmPC is listed on emc; AUDIT 2026-10-17: the IR formulation now uses the UK verapamil 80 mg tablet SPC from MHRA products (mhra-verapamil-80-tab, PL 00142/0282); the oral solution SmPC (emc-13118) is kept only for labelled general warnings and a detail item. The clinic nifedipine product (30 mg retard) has no matching UK SmPC; the once-daily 30 mg prolonged-release SmPC (emc-6180, the clinic monograph link) is used. AUDIT: the formulation note now says the doses and formulation-tied contraindications belong to the once-daily product, and a detail dosing item from a UK twice-daily retard tablet SmPC (emc-11473) is shown so the release type can be checked. Diltiazem uses only the 60 mg modified-release tablet SmPC (emc-1465); the capsule SmPCs in the clinic monograph (emc-11, emc-1293) are different products; emc-11 is used only for antihypertensive group membership and a detail indication item. Bisoprolol: both UK generic SmPCs open section 4.3 with "contraindicated in chronic heart failure patients with:". AUDIT 2026-10-17: the general contraindication rules are now sourced from a third current UK bisoprolol 5 mg SmPC (emc-14147) whose 4.3 says "contraindicated in patients with:" (all patients); the HF-only wording of emc-14905/emc-101896 is kept as a detail item. Conflicts between UK sources (kept as separate items/rules): breastfeeding - propranolol SmPC not recommended vs SPS beta-blocker of choice; bisoprolol SmPC not recommended vs SPS use with caution; diltiazem SmPC contraindicated vs SPS use with caution; verapamil SmPC only if essential vs SPS preferred; nifedipine SmPC weigh benefit vs SPS preferred. Pregnancy - SmPCs restrictive (avoid / not recommended / unless essential) vs BUMPS can be used if recommended by a doctor (beta-blockers) or nifedipine commonly used. Verapamil: oral solution SmPC 4.3 adds porphyria, IV dantrolene and grapefruit juice, which neither tablet SPC lists (AUDIT: porphyria rule is now info level, naming the oral solution as its only source). Nifedipine prolonged-release: 4.3 says not to give in hepatic impairment, while 4.4 mentions monitoring/dose reduction in impaired liver function; both recorded, rule level contraindicated. New groups: rate-limiting-ccb (verapamil, diltiazem). Added memberships: beta-blocker, calcium-channel-blocker, dihydropyridine, cyp3a4-inhibitor (verapamil, diltiazem), antihypertensive. New conditions; suggested conditionImplies for tool.json (not edited): uncontrolled-heart-failure -> heart-failure; lvf-pulmonary-stasis -> heart-failure; acute-decompensated-heart-failure -> uncontrolled-heart-failure; acute-mi-complicated -> recent-myocardial-infarction; av-block-2nd-3rd -> cardiac-conduction-disturbance; sick-sinus-syndrome -> cardiac-conduction-disturbance; severe-peripheral-arterial-disease -> peripheral-arterial-disease; severe-asthma-or-copd -> pulmonary-disease; prinzmetal-angina -> ischaemic-heart-disease; accessory-pathway-af -> cardiac-disease. No UK source fetched in this batch states a brand-prescribing requirement for nifedipine or diltiazem modified-release products, so brandPrescribing is null for all. BNF not accessed (geo-blocked). Diltiazem 4.8 table frequencies could not be read from the page text, so adverseCommon cites only the 4.7 statement (dizziness and malaise common) and lists table items without frequency; verapamil SmPCs give no frequency categories (adverseCommon not-stated). AUDIT 2026-10-17: diltiazem removed from qt-prolonging (SPS list does not include it; its SmPC only says it may lead to QT prolongation when given with QT-prolonging drugs; the diltiazem -> group:qt-prolonging interaction rule is kept). New sources: emc-14147 (bisoprolol), mhra-verapamil-80-tab (verapamil IR), emc-11473 (nifedipine retard comparison). See scripts/medcheck-uk/audit/N-O.md.
